title: Mexico and Peru Restore Diplomatic Relations
author: SinEmbargo Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by the SinEmbargo editorial staff originally appeared in
the[August 7, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4850798/mexico-y-peru-restablecen-
relaciones-diplomaticas-betsy-chavez-obtiene-salvoconducto/), one of Mexico’s
leading independent digital news outlets._

**Mexico City, August 7 (SinEmbargo).—** Mexico’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs
(SRE) reported this Friday that the governments of Mexico and Peru agreed to
resume diplomatic relations between the two nations as of today.

In a statement, the Mexican Foreign Ministry stressed that the decision to
resume the diplomatic tie between the two nations was made “considering the
historic bonds of brotherhood, friendship, and cooperation that unite them.”

In addition, the governments of the two countries reaffirmed their respect for
international law and for the principles established in the Charter of the
United Nations.

For its part, the Peruvian foreign ministry shared a post on its official
social media accounts to announce the resumption of diplomatic relations
between Mexico and Peru.

During this Friday’s “people’s mañanera,” President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo
reported that Betssy Chávez, Peru’s former Prime Minister, will arrive in
Mexico this morning after being granted safe conduct.

> It is a gesture of good will from President Fujimori’s government toward
> Mexico, and with this, relations with Peru will be restored, and we, as
> always, as we have done, will continue defending President Castillo.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

The head of the Executive recalled that Betsy Chávez remained for several
months as an asylee inside Mexico’s Embassy in Peru; however, after the
diplomatic mission was closed following the rupture of relations, the former
Peruvian official remained under the protection of the Government of Brazil.
